ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

An allergic ocular presentation

A 19-year-old student develops bilateral itchy, watery eyes each spring when pollen counts rise. There is no eye pain, visual change or purulent discharge. A clinician recommends ketotifen eye drops. Which symptom is this formulation intended to relieve?

  1. Loss of visual acuity from retinal detachment
  2. Allergy-associated ocular itching
  3. Pain from acute angle-closure glaucoma
  4. Corneal injury from a retained foreign body
  5. Purulent bacterial keratitis
Answer and explanation

Allergy-associated ocular itching

Ophthalmic ketotifen is used for allergic eye itching; the described symptoms support that indication.

Option explanations

Allergy-associated ocular itching: Ophthalmic ketotifen is used for allergic eye itching; the described symptoms support that indication.

Pain from acute angle-closure glaucoma: Painful visual symptoms need urgent assessment rather than an allergy-drop substitution.

Corneal injury from a retained foreign body: Ketotifen does not remove a foreign body or treat corneal injury.

Purulent bacterial keratitis: This requires different assessment and treatment.

Loss of visual acuity from retinal detachment: Allergy drops do not treat a retinal emergency.
